title: Semi-retirement and Nyack jazz
summary: Moore explains he is semi-retired, staying home and playing occasionally.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x:
When did you go into semi-retirement?
How long ago?

It's only a couple of years. It got to the point where I was more needed around home, and they'll be away because Ida is teaching and the kids are grown up/and Randy is living in Brooklyn and Amy is working and there's nobody to be around home here and I do odds and ends around here like I do a little gardening and take care of the lawn, do odds and ends and I've got enough to do here and when I finished with that I just want to stay home, I'm getting to be the stay-at-home type and I don't want to take long trips any more. I enjoy home life so much.

I understand you're part of the Nyack Jass scene, you play down at the Coven Cafe.
Yeah, well, they're small clubs. They're not able to support big-time people and once in a while at The Office, that's the big spot here for the men like, jazz men like --
Well, Art Farmer is coming. Cedar Walton will be here next weekend.
Stan Getz was here at one time, they're pretty cool but I have some other things to do in the City when I have anything to do with Lanin.
So when you do things with Lanin?

Sometimes I go in the city just to renew old acquaintances and listen to all the musicians play. I always get invited to play, but I won't play. I want to listen. So I enjoy myself. I haven't completely stopped playing because I love to play. I love to watch them hear me play. I love to play.
And you'll be playing tomorrow night.

Yes, I'm going up to New Hampshire to play in one of the big ballrooms up there with Lester, they like me up there and they used to stop dancing, it's so flattering for them just to stand around and listen to me.
